title: Implicit heading references
alternative: Use explicit fragment links such as `[the section](#section-id)` and assign a stable `{#section-id}` to the heading.

title: List markers and starting numbers
alternative: Use decimal markers (`1.`), including repeated `1.` for automatic numbering. Add `{type=A start=3}` after a list for alphabetic markers and a chosen start. Parenthesized marker styling may require CSS.

title: Numbered examples and cross-references
alternative: Use ordinary numbered lists with explicit starts, or write example numbers with paragraph IDs and links. There is no shared automatic example counter or `(@label)` resolver.

title: Simple tables
alternative: Rewrite using the built-in MultiMarkdown pipe-table syntax. Start with the separator row for a headerless table and put captions in square brackets.

title: Multiline tables
alternative: Use MultiMarkdown pipe tables. A trailing backslash joins source lines into one row and permits block content in cells. Captions and headerless tables are supported; ordinary text also wraps to the available width.

title: Grid tables
alternative: Use MultiMarkdown tables: adjacent pipes for column spans, ^^ for row spans, trailing backslashes for lists or code in cells, multiple header rows, and blank lines for separate tbody sections. Only a semantic tfoot still requires explicit HTML-element directives.

title: Pipe-table separator variant
alternative: Use the usual pipe-table separator row with vertical bars instead of plus signs.

title: Pandoc title blocks
alternative: Use YAML front matter and display its values with `{{ title }}`, `{{ author }}` and `{{ date }}`. Fold multiline values with `>-`. Man-page header/footer conventions have no automatic web equivalent.

title: Raw TeX
alternative: For citations, use Markdown bibliography references or `tp-ref` with `tp-biblio`. For the tabular example, use a pipe table or `tp-latex` (basic l/c/r columns, vertical rules and hline). This does not provide general raw-TeX conversion.

title: Raw output-format attributes
alternative: Use native HTML-element directives for HTML output. There is no ms/roff or OpenXML/DOCX writer. Rewrite the desired web content; CSS `break-before: page` is only a print-page-break approximation.

title: Mathematics and LaTeX macros
alternative: Enable `extensions: [math]` in YAML front matter and use a math fence, or use `tp-math` with a `script` of type `tp/latex`. Keep a macro declaration inside the formula that uses it.

title: Anonymous inline notes
alternative: Give the note a name and use `[^detail]` with a `[^detail]:` definition; add `::notes{}` for a visible list and link targets. For rich previews, use `tp-ref` with `tp-note`. Do not mix their independent numbering systems.

title: Author suppression and narrative citations
alternative: Write the author name explicitly and use `[@key]` with its bibliography definition and `::bibliography{}`, or `tp-ref`/`tp-biblio`. There is no automatic author–date formatting or author suppression. Simple citation groups are already supported.

title: Spaced reference links
alternative: Remove the space between the label and reference: `[foo][bar]`, with a normal `[bar]: URL` definition.

title: MultiMarkdown title blocks
alternative: Use YAML front matter, then `{{ title }}`, `{{ author }}`, `{{ date }}` and `{{ comment }}` in the body. Use `>-` for a folded multiline comment.

title: Abbreviation definitions
alternative: Use `:abbr:HTML{title="Hypertext Markup Language"}` or `tp-ref` with `tp-glossary`. Occurrences must be marked explicitly. Pandoc itself only discards the declaration; it does not automatically expand abbreviations.

title: Alerts
alternative: Place a `tp-callout` inside a Markdown blockquote, prefixing each directive and content line with `>`. Select its variant and heading explicitly.

title: MultiMarkdown image-reference attributes
alternative: Use an inline image URL with attributes immediately after it: `![image](image.svg){width=20 height=30}`.

title: Unclosed superscripts and subscripts
alternative: Use paired markers: `x^2^` and `O~2~`.

title: Wiki links
alternative: Use ordinary Markdown links such as `[title](destination)`. Supply the real destination; TP does not resolve wiki page names automatically.
